title: Fractions: real AQA questions
sub: An optional extra for Week 3. Every question below is from a real AQA GCSE Maths Higher paper (non-calculator). About 25 minutes on screen, then the written paper.
target: AQA gives method marks (M1) for working you write down, even if the final answer slips. Show every step, and give the answer in the form the question asks for.

sections.sub: Week 3, from memory. Cancel first if you can, and simplify fully.

blocks.why: Cancel first: 3 goes into 9, so [[2/3]] × [[9/10]] becomes [[2/1]] × [[3/10]] = [[6/10]] = [[3/5]]. Or multiply then simplify: [[18/30]] = [[3/5]].

sections.sub: Do the working on paper, type the answer. Open the mark scheme to see where the marks are.

traps.msg: You multiplied by 3. Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by [[1/3]].
You multiplied by 3. Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by [[1/3]].

blocks.q:
Work out the value of ([[3/2]])²
Give your answer as a mixed number.
blocks.formMsg: 9/4 is the right value, but the question asks for a mixed number. AQA gave 0 marks for 9/4 here.
blocks.ms:
[[2 1/4]] B1
Writing two answers on the answer line (e.g. 2¼ and 9/4, or 2¼ and 2.25) scores 0. Pick one.

blocks.q:
Work out the value of ([[1 2/3]])²
Circle your answer.
blocks.why: Change to an improper fraction first: [[1 2/3]] = [[5/3]]. Then [[5/3]] × [[5/3]] = [[25/9]] = [[2 7/9]]. (1 4/9 comes from squaring the whole and the fraction separately. That never works.)

blocks.q:
[[3/5]] of a number is 162
Work out the number.

steps.p: If 3 fifths are 162, what is one fifth?
So what is the whole number (five fifths)?

traps.msg: That is [[3/5]] of 162. Here 162 is the part, not the whole. AQA gave 0 marks for 97.2.

blocks.q: In each box, write a fraction less than 1 to make a correct calculation.
blocks.why: There are many answers: [[1/2]] × [[3/5]], [[3/4]] × [[2/5]], [[1/3]] × [[9/10]]… Multiply the tops to get 3 (or a multiple) and the bottoms to get 10 (or the same multiple).
blocks.ms:
Two fractions less than 1 with product [[3/10]], e.g. [[1/2]] and [[3/5]] B1
Decimals inside the fractions (e.g. 0.6/1) score B0.

blocks.q:
Work out [[8 1/2]] ÷ [[2 2/3]]
Give your answer as a mixed number.

steps.p: Dividing by [[8/3]] is the same as multiplying by…?

steps.hint: Tops times tops, bottoms times bottoms.

steps.p: Write it as a mixed number.
steps.hint: How many 16s go into 51? What is left over?

blocks.ms:
Convert both mixed numbers to improper fractions ([[17/2]] or [[8/3]]) M1
[[17/2]] × [[3/8]] (multiply by the reciprocal) M1
[[51/16]] A1
[[3 3/16]] B1ft (ft: a correct conversion of your own improper fraction still gets this mark)

blocks.html: Print the written paper. Two more real AQA questions, each mixing two operations. The trap is the order: brackets first, then ÷ or ×, then + or −. Mark scheme on the last page.

items: I changed mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying or squaring.
To divide, I multiplied by the reciprocal.
I gave the answer in the form asked (mixed number / fraction).
I wrote one answer only on the answer line.
I checked one answer by estimating or working backwards.

blocks.q: “What is [[1 2/3]] squared, and why isn’t it [[1 4/9]]?”
blocks.note: For the parent: listen for “change it to 5/3 first, then 5/3 × 5/3 = 25/9”.

paper.title: Maths Week 3 plus: fractions (written)
paper.sub: Ember · Real AQA GCSE Maths Higher questions (non-calculator) · about 15 minutes
paper.intro: Skill: written method and checking. Write every step. Method marks (M1) are for working you can see. Under each answer, write a check: an estimate, or work backwards.

blocks.q:
Work out   ([[7/10]] − [[4/15]]) ÷ [[2/3]]
Give your answer as a fraction.

Work out   [[4/15]] + [[1/5]] ÷ [[1/2]]
Give your answer as a fraction.

blocks.html:
Check: ________________________________________________

Before you mark: in the second question, which did you do first, the + or the ÷? Why?

selfcheck: I did the bracket first in the first question.
I did the ÷ before the + in the second question.
I found a common denominator before adding or subtracting.
To divide, I multiplied by the reciprocal.
My answers are fractions (not decimals), and I wrote a check under each.

marking.h: AQA mark scheme: November 2022, Q8 (3 marks)
marking.html:
• Valid common denominator for the subtraction, with at least one numerator correct, e.g. [[21/30]] − [[8/30]] or [[13/30]] M1
  • their [[13/30]] × [[3/2]] M1
  • [[13/20]] or [[39/60]] (or an equivalent fraction) A1
A correct fraction in your working but a decimal on the answer line scores M2 A0. Score: ____ / 3

marking.h: AQA mark scheme: June 2025, Q8 (3 marks)
marking.html:
• Correct method to divide by [[1/2]] (implied by [[2/5]] or 0.4) M1
  • Correct method to add two fractions with different denominators M1
  • [[2/3]] (or an equivalent fraction, e.g. [[10/15]]) A1
Division comes before addition, so [[1/5]] ÷ [[1/2]] = [[2/5]] first, then [[4/15]] + [[6/15]] = [[10/15]] = [[2/3]]. Score: ____ / 3
